items.definition: Not able to find the way home. If you are lost, you are not in trouble. You just need help.
items.example: Pip was lost, but he was not frightened of the dark.

items.definition: A smell that hangs in the air. Dogs can smell scents and follow them a long way.
items.example: Pip knew the scent of his own garden.

items.definition: The band that goes around a dog's neck. It can hold a small tag with the dog's name.
items.example: Mum put Pip's name on his new collar.

items.definition: The home of a bear. It is a cave with a door, and it is warm inside.
items.example: Bo's den had a wooden door.

items.definition: What really happened, even when it is not the easy thing to say.
items.example: An told his mother the truth about the blue bowl.

items.definition: Saying something you know is not true, on purpose, to make things easier for yourself.
items.example: He could have said the wind broke the bowl, but that would be a lie.

items.definition: Something you say you will do. People remember a broken promise for a long time.
items.example: An promised to tell his mother everything from then on.

items.definition: Not feeling no fear, but going on anyway. Brave is about what you do, not what you feel.
items.example: Pip was brave and took one more step.

items.definition: The yearly price of borrowing on the card, with most fees included. It is the number to compare two cards by.
items.example: This card has a 24 % APR, which is about 0.066 % a day.

items.definition: The most the bank will let you borrow on the card at one time. Going over it is usually refused and sometimes charged.
items.example: My credit limit is 2000 $, and I use about 600 $ of it.

items.definition: The period between two statements. Everything bought in one cycle appears on the next statement.
items.example: The billing cycle closes on the 12th, so my groceries appear on the 12th statement.

items.definition: The days between the statement date and the due date, during which you can pay in full without interest.
items.example: If I pay the statement balance inside the grace period, I pay no interest.

items.definition: The smallest monthly sum the card will accept. Paying only this keeps the balance, and the interest, alive.
items.example: The minimum payment is 25 $, so the rest of the balance stays on the card.

items.definition: The charge the bank makes for a late payment, on top of any penalty rate and any loss of your good history.
items.example: The late payment cost me a 35 $ overdue fee and my standard rate went up.

items.definition: The percentage change in the general level of prices over a period of time, usually a year.
items.example: The annual inflation rate was 4 %, so prices rose 4 % on average.

items.definition: The standard index of the price of a basket of goods and services bought by households. Its change over time is the headline inflation rate.
items.example: The consumer price index is the number the news report quotes.

items.definition: The year the price index starts from, set to 100. Changing it resets the index without changing any actual prices.
items.example: With last year as the base year, the index now stands at 104.

items.definition: Income measured in the money actually received, with no adjustment for changes in prices.
items.example: My nominal income rose, but not as fast as prices.

items.definition: Income adjusted for inflation, which is the figure that says how much you can actually buy.
items.example: Real income fell two per cent because prices rose faster than my pay.

items.definition: The interest rate minus the inflation rate. It is the return a saver actually keeps in purchasing power.
items.example: A 4 % deposit with 6 % inflation gives a real interest rate of minus 2 %.

items.definition: Total pay for the period before any money is deducted for tax, insurance or other agreed deductions.
items.example: My gross pay is 40 $ a month, before anything is taken off.

items.definition: The amount left after all deductions, and the amount that reaches your bank account.
items.example: The difference between my gross and my net is mostly tax and insurance.

items.definition: Any amount taken off gross pay before payment, whether required by law or agreed with you.
items.example: The canteen charge is a deduction, so it comes out before my net pay.

items.definition: Income tax taken out of your pay in advance by the employer. It is not your final tax bill.
items.example: The tax withheld this month was higher because my bonus was large.

items.definition: The compulsory payment into the social insurance system that covers sickness, maternity, accidents and retirement.
items.example: My social insurance contribution is a percentage of my gross pay.

items.definition: Money you paid for work that the company owes you back. It almost always needs a receipt and a deadline.
items.example: I submitted the taxi receipts as an expense claim on Friday.

items.definition: A line you draw around your time, energy, body or values, and say out loud so other people can respect it.
items.example: Her boundary was simple: no phone calls after ten.

items.definition: The point at which you stop giving: the time, the amount or the effort. A limit is the measurable side of a boundary.
items.example: My limit is two favours a week, and I stick to it.

items.definition: Something a person asks of you. A request deserves an answer; it does not deserve obedience.
items.example: The request was reasonable, and the answer was still no.

items.definition: To have to have something.
The act of saying no to something. It is a decision about an offer, not a verdict on a person.
items.example: She declined the invitation politely and without drama.

items.definition: The result you decide to bring about when a boundary is crossed. It is chosen by you, and it should be small and repeatable.
items.example: Her consequence was simple: she stopped answering messages late at night.

items.definition: An intense feeling of attraction for someone you have not yet got close to.
items.example: I have a crush on someone from my office, but we have only ever said hello.

items.definition: A planned meeting with someone you are getting to know. It implies time set aside for each other.
items.example: Is Friday a date, or just a coffee between friends?

items.definition: A relationship that has no agreed label. Nobody has said what it is, and nobody has asked.
items.example: We have been seeing each other for months and calling it a situationship.

items.definition: Stopping all contact without explanation, so the other person is left waiting and guessing.
items.example: He replied for three weeks and then ghosted me completely.

items.definition: Sending occasional messages to keep someone interested while never making any real plan.
items.example: He messages me every few days but has never once suggested meeting.

items.definition: Someone you were in a relationship with and are no longer in one.
items.example: My ex and I still share a group of friends, so we keep it simple.

items.definition: When one person's behaviour and words point in different directions, usually because they are unsure or unwilling to say where things stand.
items.example: He texts every day but has cancelled three plans — those are mixed signals.

items.definition: Everyone agreeing freely to something, every time. A clear no is a complete answer that needs no follow-up.
items.example: Consent has to be clear on both sides, and a no is always a complete answer.
